lesson.grammar_point: used to and would for past habits

listenings.text: Luiz, it's Almir. You asked me about this desk in 1988, so here it is. We used to wait eleven days for one credit decision, and it needed three signatures. I would drive out to two farms every week, and I would sit in the kitchen until somebody made coffee. The contracts used to live in a locked room, and we checked that room once a year. Credit used to come at the end of the process. Now it comes near the beginning. One thing did not change. They still pay after the harvest.

Luiz, Megan again. They want two lines from me for the anniversary booklet, and you know this desk better than I do, so tell me if these are right. A credit decision used to take eleven days, and now it takes about forty minutes. Analysts used to visit two customers a week, and now most weeks they visit none. I would rather be accurate than warm. If one of those numbers is wrong, send me the right one by Friday.
